revisions.rationale: The original artifact reports the primary arm below both pass bars (CAGR 14.1871% versus SPY 14.8294%, difference -0.6423 pp/year; Newey-West t -0.6898). The approved closure records the historical model NO-GO; it is preserved. A later audit found incorrect PARA identity with unmeasured impact, so the validity of the primary result and the affected protocol determination remain unresolved under the new framework. After-tax was not triggered. Lens 9 estimated a 4.24 pp/year detectable effect for annualized mean excess under its assumptions, not a CAGR confidence interval; no inference of no modest benefit follows.
revisions.uncertainties: The primary passed its registered data detector, not a full price-identity verification. Later audit identified incorrect PARA prices and did not establish their return impact; no new validity clearance or causal effect is inferred. The audit MDE is for annualized mean excess, not a confidence bound on the CAGR gap. The closure amendment was approved after results; its NO-GO scope is distinct from the original stopped raw run.

revisions.rationale: Coverage 87.39% exceeded the 70% floor, but the registered tainted-trade stop triggered: 21 trade/artifact matches represent 11 distinct symbol-date trades; remaining sensitivity arms were not run. The original INCONCLUSIVE verdict is preserved; the framework evidence label UNRESOLVED reflects the data fault.
revisions.uncertainties: Flags are not proof every move is false: RHT may reflect a genuine corporate event; mixed identity in TIE/MEE is an inference. Detector limitations and survivorship risk remain; holdout performance is not investment evidence.

A1 uses 1927-01–2026-04, NW(12), and 1%/3% annual base haircuts. Original NO-GO and closure follow the stated two-gate rule. The numerical policy outcome is preserved; prior registration of the timing-sensitive prospective claim is unverified.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 9 cannot compute an effect-size MDE from the stored artifact; power and effects ruled out are unknown. The audit calls registration late: the brief and results first appear in the same commit, so prior commitment cannot be verified. French portfolios compare with French market, not SPY; fixed haircuts are not realized costs or tax and do not test a stock-level implementation.

revisions.rationale: All four fail both gates: first Holm-ranked H4 p=0.090310 exceeds 0.0003375; A2 1994-01–2026-04 net CAGR differences H1 +0.826675, H2 -0.620700, H3 -0.000702, H4 -0.559214 pp/yr each miss +1.0. A1 is 1963-07–2026-04, NW(12), family alpha 0.00135; annual base haircuts 1% H1–H3, 1.5% H4. Original NO-GO and closure follow the registered two-gate rule.

revisions.rationale: The frozen static-arm bar was met: pinned 2021-02-01–2026-04-30 Sharpe 0.973 vs SPY 0.896 and MaxDD −21.3% vs −24.5%; 2016-01-04–2026-04-30 Sharpe 0.967 vs 0.872 and MaxDD −28.4% vs −33.7%; 2022 return −15.8% vs −18.6%; checks held at 3 bp and under each single-leg removal. CAGR lagged SPY by 1.1 pp/yr on both windows. These are original policy checks, not statistical support for defensive benefit. The post-hoc pinned Sharpe-gap 90% CI was [−0.02,+0.18]; long-window CI [+0.03,+0.16] is post-hoc and neither is a registered downside/wealth noninferiority joint test. Preserve the original GO-for-shadow result; no approved forward scope is evidenced here.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 1 calls the static headline clean; Lens 2/Lens 9 cannot compute interval or MDE from the artifact's CAGR/Sharpe fields. Both pinned and long windows were inspected in the prior sanity check; the bootstrap is post-hoc and DESCRIPTIVE, not untouched prospective evidence. Tax, after-tax wealth, broader crisis coverage, and a forward shadow are not established. Report table begins 2021-02-01, while raw JSON metadata begins 2021-01-31.

revisions.rationale: The separately frozen 2007-06-01–2011-02-28 holdout met its restricted checks: static 80/20 with DBC had Sharpe 0.172 vs SPY 0.078 and MaxDD −46.3% vs −55.2%; results held at 3 bp. Its brief explicitly calls this weak support because the roughly 3.75-year span is dominated by 2008, likely to flatter the mix. It does not establish material downside improvement plus wealth noninferiority. Preserve PASSED (weak); protocol MET is not proof of persistent defensive effect. The report records CAGR 1.3% versus -1.7% and 2008 total return -29.9% versus -36.8% for SPY.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 1 calls the holdout clean and Lens 7 spot-checked recomputation. Lens 6 is unverifiable; Lens 9 cannot compute t-statistic, uncertainty, or MDE. The report records that SPY differed from the OHLCV tape on one overlap day outside the holdout. The period is limited and does not cover varied adverse regimes. The holdout brief states that data from 2011-03 onward had already been seen.

revisions.rationale: The registered trend-preference rule was not met: pinned trend improvement over static was only +0.007 Sharpe and +1.6 MaxDD points versus required +0.05 Sharpe or +3 points without Sharpe loss; WFO halted in folds 2–8, violating the no-halt condition. Long-window trend Sharpe was below static (0.948 vs 0.967). This supports the original narrow conclusion that this timing arm adds nothing over static under its rule, not a general absence of defensive value. The original closure is preserved. The report gives 14/17 WFO gate passes and lookback 126 winning 8/17. The clean pinned comparison alone fails the necessary first condition, independently of uncertain WFO validity.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 1 says pinned comparison is clean but WFO validity is unknown (it predates an engine fix); Lens 2 records DSR-unit uncertainty, code unverifiable, and no MDE; Lens 9 cannot compute uncertainty. NOT MET is the registered policy/operational outcome; broad inference is inconclusive.

The tested question is isolated commodity trend/filter versus SPY, not commodity diversification against a fixed passive allocation. Carry and basis-reversal legs were outside scope and remain untested.

The unhedged reference was 0.53 Sharpe, 9.7% CAGR and -35.2% MaxDD; SPY reference was 0.74, 15.2% and -33.7%.
revisions.uncertainties: The academic claim and report comparator are dynamic versus static FX hedge policies; SPY is reference-only. The available JPY/EUR ETF proxy history does not test the broader strategy. The audit found no raw artifact, so values were not independently recomputed. No owner-approved continuation is evidenced.

revisions.rationale: The source reports the top-11 Binance.US run had zero full-cascade passers; the all-51 Binance.US run had two marginal passers and +13.8% CAGR versus BTC +38.8%; and the Kraken top-100 run returned -10.0%. The report says no passer had a clean, trade-rich positive holdout and closes the cheap gate, universe, and venue/fee levers. Preserve the original “no deployable edge” verdict and this bounded scope. Lens 8 says the Binance.US tape includes 44% Kraken copies, flags survivorship, and notes the headline venue flip is confounded by universe, tape, selected coins, and fees. The underlying raw results are absent from the repository and Lens 2 reports data unknown, no raw artifact, and no pre-registered brief. These prevent independent validation of the inference and registered protocol result; they do not establish that every crypto strategy lacks an edge.
revisions.uncertainties: Reported values are sourced to the 2026-06-08 report and Lens 8 reanalysis; no raw results were independently recomputed. Binance.US copied-bar provenance, survivorship and confounded venue comparison limit causal interpretation. The source tested long-only spot WFO in the listed universes and venues; it did not test directional shorting, broader crypto strategies or a longer history.

revisions.rationale: The Phase 4 report describes a delta-neutral long-spot/short-PF_XBTUSD funding-carry test. Its real-funding run reports +0.45%, Sharpe 4.44 and 8 trades over 2025-05-15–2026-05-15; the report itself limits the basis proxy as not quotable and notes zero trade-event overlap between the real-funding and proxy runs. Lens 8 confirms the results are prose-only, with inputs and legacy code noted as existing, but no raw result artifact is available; Lens 2 found no brief or registered bar. Preserve the original cautious verdict. Numerical evidence and the registered protocol determination cannot be independently checked without a raw result and a registered brief; unknown power alone is not the reason for UNRESOLVED. The quoted cautious verdict refers specifically to basis-proxy B; the report treats real-funding A separately as its canonical quotable result.
revisions.uncertainties: No results artifact or pre-registration was located. The report’s input dataset and legacy code are described in the source and Lens 8, but this annotation does not access the database or reconstruct the run. One year of real funding data and eight trades are thin; the basis proxy differs in trade timing and is not a valid substitute.

revisions.rationale: The original finding is a descriptive split of IBIT ETF session returns, not a registered strategy test. The JSON artifact reports separate intraday, weeknight and weekend statistics; Lens 2 notes no benchmark series, no registered bar, and that `overnight_all` lacks a t-statistic, so it selected the three available sub-rows for partial recomputation. Lens 8 says the crypto Sharpe annualization issue does not affect these total-return results. Preserve the source’s “closed in practice — do not build” action. Because there is no registered decision rule and the artifact’s selected statistic does not match a single declared verdict arm, protocol determination is unresolved; the descriptive split does not establish a deployable edge.
revisions.uncertainties: This artifact concerns IBIT (a US-listed ETF), despite its crypto inventory grouping. It tests absolute session returns, not excess returns versus a benchmark. The audit’s iid t-statistics and post-hoc selection are descriptive; the window, session counts and means do not resolve whether the pattern persists or is tradeable.

The old engine’s removal is recorded history, not an action recommendation about the project.
revisions.uncertainties: Trade records, the source P&L script, starting/ending capital and full external cash-flow-adjusted return are unavailable. The capital injection makes the dollar figure unsuitable as a performance rate; no inference about profitability follows.

revisions.rationale: The closure report records a same-universe, same-grid fee sweep with 36, 14, 13 and 0 aggregate-gate passers from frictionless through Kraken taker costs, and states that zero coins formed a portfolio in every variant. Lens 8 found the inventory’s cited raw artifact points to the frictionless run rather than the realistic-fee run; the latter’s gate count is reconstructed from worker logs, and no portfolio formed even at zero cost. Lens 2 reports no registered brief, no excess-vs-benchmark statistic, and unverified code. Preserve the original closed result and the narrow WFO/fee-sweep scope. The mispointed artifact, incomplete durable evidence and missing registered brief prevent an independent determination of the affected protocol and portfolio claims.
revisions.uncertainties: The closure report is detailed, but the realistic-fee raw snapshot was not preserved at the cited location; Lens 8 says the stated zero-pass count is available in worker logs. Do not conflate the aggregate gate-pass counts with deployable portfolios or with the separate venue/migration decision. Crypto data provenance and survivorship concerns remain under Lens 8; no new computation was done.

revisions.rationale: The registered primary criteria were after-tax CAGR ≥ SPY +1.0 pp/year on the 2006-06-21–2026-09-29 real-SSO window and not below SPY on the 1993-02-01–2006-06-20 synthetic holdout. The report records the 70/30 arm clearing both using the historical financing path; its 2026-09-30 +2.5 pp funding-cost sensitivity reduces the main-window margin to +0.80 pp/year, below the same +1.0 bar. Preserve GO for owner decision and the documented owner adoption of 1.3x; the sensitivity does not authorize changing the allocation. Lens 2 found clean data and recomputation, but code was not examined and Lens 9 could not compute power because the stored artifact lacks the needed uncertainty inputs. The historical result and current funding condition are distinct determinations; no alpha inference is intended.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 9 could not compute MDE/power from the stored result fields; this is absence of a computable effect-size uncertainty estimate, not evidence of zero power or invalidity by itself. Lens 6 has no code review row. The report identifies these as already-seen windows; moreover the synthetic holdout uses a financing spread calibrated on later real SSO returns and so is not untouched OOS. The +2.5 pp funding sensitivity was a historical scenario dated 2026-09-30, not a current market measurement. The comparison is an allocation-risk study with substantially deeper drawdowns, not stock-selection alpha.

revisions.rationale: The registered rule returns keep 30% because no alternative passes all four conditions. On the primary 24%/15% path, 30% has 10.71% full-window after-tax CAGR versus 9.47% at 0%, but reaches −91.4% drawdown and trips the −90% ruin flag; 15% reaches −87.9% but is 0.54 pp/year below 30%, failing the required +0.5 pp/year improvement over 30%. The report states 0%, 15%, 45%, and 60% also fail at least one of the four criteria. Preserve keep 30% as advice for the 2027-09-30 review only, despite the identified rule limitation that it may retain a ruin-flagged incumbent. Lens 2 found clean data and recomputation but code unexamined and power uncomputable; the inferential/evidence status remains INCONCLUSIVE.
revisions.uncertainties: Lens 9 cannot compute MDE/power from the available artifact; the report’s decision is a deterministic registered recommendation rule, so missing power alone does not invalidate that rule outcome. Lens 6 did not examine code. Data are proxy/synthetic: French all-US market is not S&P 500; the synthetic 2x leg is calibrated on modern overlap and carried backward, with no historical fund failure, margin/counterparty risk, or verified historical financing. Tax rates are current-law hypotheticals; synthetic 2x distributions are zero. The rule checks ruin on the full window only. The 30% arm trips ruin and no alternative meets all gates; this is a design limitation explicitly described by the report, not a rationale to alter the dated action.

Below-30 proposal additionally requires 30% itself trips ruin or trails 0% full-window CAGR. Otherwise advise keep 30%; this is review advice only, not trade authorization.

revisions.rationale: Two records must remain distinct. The June 12 changelog entry covers a 64-month 2021-02–2026-05 top-50 run: it calls dual_momentum “vacuous at this book size” because the negative-momentum filter never fired, with minimum selected momentum +12.2% in October 2022. Separately, the corrected replay artifact `research/audits/production-replica/_audit_reruns_20261019.json` covers 2021-01-31–2026-04-30 and contains a `dual_momentum` record: t=0.7606, CAGR difference +4.3674 pp/year, t bar 3.0, CAGR bar +1.0 pp/year, 0/17 gates, and anchor used in every fold. Thus the recorded protocol result is NOT MET (the t and WFO gate conditions fail; the CAGR difference alone clears its bar). Lens 2 found clean inputs and matching code; the effect-size MDE is 22.66 pp/year at t≥3, far above +1.0 pp/year, so evidence is INCONCLUSIVE rather than evidence against all smaller effects. The corrected replay artifact contains aggregate statistics, not daily return observations for a new independent recomputation. Preserve each decision at its own window and scope; neither record establishes that the dual filter adds value on another book size or period.
revisions.uncertainties: The +12.2% minimum and “vacuous” statement belong only to the June 12 64-month top-50 record. The October corrected replay is separately represented in the preserved aggregate JSON, but its daily OOS return series is not available here for independent recomputation. Lens 9’s MDE is for annualized mean excess, not a CAGR confidence interval; power is too weak to resolve the +1.0 pp/year hurdle. The French portfolio momentum screen is another distinct specification.
